question.text: SEBI's power to suspend business of recognized stock exchanges comes under:

explanation.text: The Logic: Page 259 of the NISM XV workbook states that the Securities Contracts (Regulation) Act, 1956 provides control over various aspects of the securities market, and page 260 specifically lists the power to suspend business of recognized stock exchanges. The Trap: While the SEBI Act provides general regulatory powers, the specific power to suspend business of a recognized stock exchange is derived from the SC(R)A, 1956. Note: Source-backed by NISM Series XV Research Analyst Workbook (February 2026), pages 259-260.
